content:
Data Handling looks like the easiest chapter in Class 7. Then the IMO asks for the median of an even-sized list. Or the probability of "at least one head". That is when careful practice shows. The free IMO Class 7 Data Handling online test below has 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Treat it as a diagnostic. Every explanation tells you what to revise.

What the IMO asks from Data Handling in Class 7

  • Mean, median and mode (including even-sized lists).
  • Range and organising data.
  • Reading and drawing bar graphs and double bar graphs.
  • Chance and probability basics.
  • Choosing the right average for a situation.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Median of an even count = average of the two middle values (after sorting!).
  • Mean changes if EVERY value changes; mode only cares about frequency.
  • Probability = favourable/total: a die shows a prime with probability 3/6 = 1/2.
  • Range = maximum − minimum — a spread measure, not an average.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Finding the median without sorting first.
  • Averaging two averages without weighting by group sizes.
  • Counting 1 as a prime when listing die outcomes.

questions.q: Buying a market-research report on teenagers' screen time and using its figures means using:
questions.explanation: The investigator did not collect it first-hand. Pre-existing published data is secondary.

The mean weight of 9 students is 45 kg. A 55-kg student joins. The new mean is:
Each observation of a data set with mean x̄ is multiplied by k and then increased by m. The new mean is:
questions.explanation: The mean follows the same operations as the data. New mean = kx̄ + m.

questions.q: The median of the first 9 prime numbers is:
questions.explanation: The first 9 primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23. With 9 values the median is the 5th one: 11.

questions.q: A bag has 5 red, 8 blue and 7 green marbles. P(neither red nor green) is:
questions.explanation: Neither red nor green = blue: 8 of 20. 8/20 = 2/5.
